attacker_pocs.name: dfa_workspace_reuse
attacker_pocs.cmd: cmake -S . -B /tmp/pcre2-asan-fixture -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS='-O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer' -DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS='-fsanitize=address' -DPCRE2_BUILD_PCRE2_16=OFF -DPCRE2_BUILD_PCRE2_32=OFF -DPCRE2_BUILD_TESTS=OFF -DPCRE2_SUPPORT_JIT=OFF >/tmp/pcre2-fixture-configure.log && cmake --build /tmp/pcre2-asan-fixture --target pcre2-8-static -j4 >/tmp/pcre2-fixture-build.log && cc -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -I src pocs/residual.c /tmp/pcre2-asan-fixture/libpcre2-8.a -o /tmp/pcre2-residual-fixture && ASAN_OPTIONS=halt_on_error=1 /tmp/pcre2-residual-fixture
attacker_pocs.why: Nested lookaheads allocate a heap-limited DFA workspace block; a later recursive call needs a larger offset vector and reuses that undersized block. The shipped change makes new-block heap accounting overflow-safe but does not check the size of an existing next block before reuse. The upstream fix checks it and returns PCRE2_ERROR_HEAPLIMIT.

role_a_rationale: The commit fixes overflow-prone doubling and heap allowance arithmetic in more_workspace(), using the project's existing error path and formatting. It omits the upstream size check on an existing next workspace block. The public API reproducer causes that single residual heap buffer overflow under AddressSanitizer, while the upstream tree returns the heap-limit error.
